title: Chapter 238: Found You!
html:
“The brighter the girl shone, the more fiercely the others envied her. She did nothing to provoke them, yet they ostracized her all the same. Sometimes, being favored by God is no blessing. Most people, after all, are demons.

“One of the five girls fell in love, and what followed was painfully ordinary. She wrote the boy a letter confessing her feelings, but he had no interest in her. He had approached her only to learn more about the talented girl.

“When she discovered the truth, envy and humiliation drove her to a mad decision. She sought out the equipment-room attendant, and together they devised a plan to destroy the girl.

“As the competition approached, all six girls practiced in the dance studio every afternoon. The school stood empty during the summer holiday. The others pretended to befriend their target, and in her innocence, she truly believed they wanted her friendship.

“She volunteered for extra chores and even made homemade sweets for her ‘friends.’

“However, she should have known it was all a trap. It was her ‘friends’ who pushed her into the depths of hell.”

No. 2 continued his story, but Chen Ge’s hands had already curled into fists.Found you!

The killer was telling his story of sin to everyone there, and there was no regret in his voice.

Zhang Ya...Chen Ge called her name inwardly. Hearing the entire story stirred a new emotion within him: heartache. His shadow changed color, but Zhang Ya did not appear. Perhaps she had consumed too many ghosts in the Third Sick Hall and was still digesting them.

As if knowing something was up, No. 2 glanced at Chen Ge.

“The girl begged her ‘friends’ for help. Instead, one of them pulled a love letter from her bag. The boy she adored had written it—but not to her.

“Cornered, the girl glanced at the window behind her. She fell from the fourth floor, and blood blossomed around her. Even then, she was beautiful.

“She remained alive but could not make a sound. Her eyes stayed open, fixed on the ‘friends’ who had abandoned her.

“Blood dyed her white ballet dress red. No one knew exactly when she died; her body was not discovered until the following day.”

With every sentence, the bloody streaks in Chen Ge’s shadow darkened. After consuming two thin monsters and much of the old director’s Red Specter, something within Zhang Ya appeared to have changed. Chen Ge had no means of summoning her. She had helped him three times, but on every occasion, she had appeared of her own accord.

“Other than the wounds from the fall, there were no other injuries on the girl’s body. With the testimonies from the ugly ducklings, her case was deemed a suicide.”

No. 2 began calmly, but as he spoke, his breathing grew ragged and his gaze kept straying toward Chen Ge. Seeming to sense something, he hurried through the fate of the five girls. Each received a mysterious love letter written in blood, then died under inexplicable circumstances one week later. Coincidentally, every body was found seated in a chair.

“The school rumor says that it’s a cursed musical chair game, but the truth is the girl has returned as a specter and has been roaming the dance studio.”

No. 2 took a step back. “That’s the end.”

“The plot is acceptable, but your pacing is a mess. You should learn from the others how to tell a proper story.” The man on the right yawned, then looked across the table. “What do you think?”

“At least it was interesting, unlike last week’s newcomer.” The first man on the left tapped the table, a cold light in his eyes. The man on the right laughed. “Since he passes, it’s No. 3’s turn.”

“Wait a minute,” the man on the left said. His gaze slowly moved away from No. 2 toward Chen Ge. “No. 2, No. 4, do you two know each other?”

Chen Ge had not expected the man to be so perceptive. With Zhang Ya still unresponsive, he could only stall for time.

“No, we don’t know each other,” No. 2 replied, equally surprised that the man had noticed his subtle reaction.

“Since you don’t know him, why did you keep looking at him both consciously and unconsciously when you told your story?”

At those words, every masked face around the table turned toward No. 2 and Chen Ge. Knife-sharp gazes pierced them.

The room grew tense. Chen Ge continued calling Zhang Ya, but she did not answer, though the streaks in his shadow deepened to a brighter red. No. 2 answered more candidly. “He makes me uneasy. A voice in my head keeps warning me that he’s dangerous.”

“Dangerous?” The masks focused on Chen Ge. “A dangerous new member?”

“Is it his mask?” asked the person who had admired it earlier. Resting his chin on one hand, he studied Chen Ge’s disguise. “It truly is a work of art. One day, it will belong to me.”

His remark at least diverted attention from Chen Ge. The first man on the left did not pursue the matter. He shrugged. “No. 3, let us hear your story.”

No. 3 was the only woman among the four newcomers. She was of average height and build.

“My surname is Zhong, and I work at a chemical plant.” The woman touched the homemade mask on her face, and her first sentence made everyone frown.

“Miss Zhong, for your own safety, please do not reveal personal information,” the man on the right warned, but she appeared unconcerned.

“The story I want to tell concerns my wife.” The woman’s voice was gentle as birdsong. “She was four years younger than me and hosted a late-night radio program.

“Her show ran from midnight until two in the morning, so she returned home late every night. When we first married, I waited up so we could fall asleep together. But because I had to work early each morning, I could only maintain that routine for a short time.

“I began cooking dinner for both of us and leaving her a note, asking her to reheat her portion when she came home.

“At first, everything was fine. Then one night, my wife stopped touching the food on the table. The next morning, it appeared untouched, yet the utensils in the kitchen showed signs of use.

“My wife seemed to be cooking in the dark.”
